observation_summary: The code throws a FractionConversionException when the next iteration of the continued fraction algorithm results in an overflow, even if the current state is already a valid approximation within the specified constraints.
hypothesis: The FractionConversionException is thrown prematurely when the continued fraction algorithm encounters an overflow in the next iteration, even if the current convergent (p1/q1) already satisfies the maxDenominator constraint and is a sufficiently accurate representation of the input value.
prediction: The fix involves adding a conditional check before throwing the exception to verify if the previous convergent (p1/q1) is within the allowed maxDenominator, effectively allowing the algorithm to terminate gracefully instead of failing.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff shows that a new conditional check (if epsilon == 0.0 && FastMath.abs(q1) < maxDenominator) was added to break the loop instead of throwing the exception. This is a classic validation/guard logic correction.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an overly aggressive guard condition that throws an exception when an overflow is detected in the *next* iteration, without checking if the *current* iteration already provides a valid result. Adding a check to validate the current state before throwing the exception is a correction of the loop termination logic/guard.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it modifies the loop, the core issue is the missing validation check (guard) that determines whether to continue or terminate, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
